Write variable names as a model formula reads them

Source: R/fit_utils.R
formula_names.Rd

The variables of fit(), uniscreen(), multifit(), and fullfit() are given as column names, from which the model formula is written as text. A column name that is not a syntactic name, such as "tumor stage", is read in a formula as code unless it is quoted with backticks. A term that is a column name, each component of an interaction term ("a:b") whose components are all column names, and each argument of a Surv() outcome that is a column name are quoted where the name requires it. A column name may also be given with backticks. Other terms, such as function calls and random effects, are kept as given, as is a term in which no name changes.

Usage

formula_names(terms, var_names, quote = TRUE)

Arguments

terms

Character vector of terms, or NULL.

var_names

Character vector of column names.

quote

Logical. If TRUE (default), names are written as a formula reads them. If FALSE, the backticks of column names are removed instead, so that the terms match the columns of the data; Surv() outcomes are then kept as given.

Value

Character vector of terms, or NULL when terms is NULL.
